correctness.rationale: Substituting d=ab and g=1+ab(a+b-4)/2 into Cayley's quadrisecant formula gives the displayed integer polynomial Q_{a,b}. A fresh exact-integer check confirmed the specialization against Cayley's formula for all 4<=a,b<=80. Symbolically, the numerator N=24Q satisfies N(a+8,b)-N(a,b)=16 b R(a,b), and bR is divisible by 3 because modulo 3 it reduces to b^2((a^3+a)b^2+a+2b^2+1), which vanishes in all residue cases; hence Q parity is 8-periodic in each degree. Exhausting the 64 residue pairs gives exactly the two stated parity rules and 24 odd classes. Complex conjugation pairs nonreal points of a real reduced zero-dimensional quadrisecant scheme, so odd complex degree forces a real line.
